title: Fortran Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Write a greeting
entries.summary: A program block holds the steps. The A format writes character text.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none

write(*,'(A)') "Hello, Asha!"
end program lesson

notes: implicit none makes you declare variable types instead of guessing them.

entries.name: Name a whole number
entries.summary: integer declares a whole-number value. The I0 format prints it without leading padding.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: pencils = 3
write(*,'(I0)') pencils + 2
end program lesson

entries.name: Use a decimal value
entries.summary: real holds a decimal value. The F3.1 format prints one digit after the decimal point.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
real :: length = 2.5
write(*,'(F3.1)') length
end program lesson

notes: Choose a wider output format for a wider number.

entries.name: Group numbers in an array
entries.summary: An array stores several values. This array has three integer positions.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 5, 8]
write(*,'(3(I0,1X))') scores
end program lesson

notes: Array sizes and initial value counts must agree.

entries.name: Read an array position
entries.summary: Fortran arrays normally start at position 1. Parentheses select an item.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 5, 8]
write(*,'(I0)') scores(2)
end program lesson

notes: Do not assume array indexing starts at zero.

entries.name: Choose a message
entries.summary: An if block runs one branch based on a logical test.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: score = 8
if (score >= 5) then
 write(*,'(A)') "Pass"
else
 write(*,'(A)') "Try again"
end if
end program lesson

notes: Close the block with end if.

entries.name: Count with do
entries.summary: A counted do loop includes both its start and end values.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: n
do n = 1, 3
 write(*,'(I0)') n
end do
end program lesson

notes: Do not change the loop counter inside the counted loop.

entries.name: Add an array
entries.summary: sum adds the values in an array. It is a built-in array operation.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: values(3) = [2, 3, 4]
write(*,'(I0)') sum(values)
end program lesson

notes: sum returns a result; it does not change the array.

entries.name: Change selected array items
entries.summary: where applies a change only where an array condition is true.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 8, 9]
where (scores >= 7) scores = scores + 1
write(*,'(3(I0,1X))') scores
end program lesson

notes: The mask and array must have compatible shapes.

entries.name: Return a calculated value
entries.summary: A function has a result. contains separates the main steps from local function definitions.

example.code:
program lesson
 implicit none
 write(*,'(I0)') twice(4)
contains
 integer function twice(n) result(answer)
  integer, intent(in) :: n
  answer = n * 2
 end function twice
end program lesson

notes: Give the function input and result explicit types.

entries.name: Change a value through a subroutine
entries.summary: A subroutine is called with call. intent(inout) means this input may be changed.

example.code:
program lesson
 implicit none
 integer :: n = 4
 call double_value(n)
 write(*,'(I0)') n
contains
 subroutine double_value(value)
  integer, intent(inout) :: value
  value = value * 2
 end subroutine double_value
end program lesson

notes: Use call for a subroutine; a function is used in an expression.

entries.name: Choose an array size at run time
entries.summary: An allocatable array gets its size when allocate runs. deallocate releases its storage.

example.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer, allocatable :: scores(:)
allocate(scores(3))
scores = 0
write(*,'(I0)') size(scores)
deallocate(scores)
end program lesson

notes: Allocate before using the array and do not use it after deallocation.
